messages:
anna kim: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to lock down how we propagate billing/join keys from traces into the cost-aggregation pipeline. observed an edge case where sampled traces lost user_org context and cost got mis-attributed.

samir patel: Can you paste the failing example?

anna kim: repro: span starts in frontend (has org_id, user_id), then enters inference mesh (model routing) which only tags model_id and request_id. sampling happened after mesh so sampled trace had no org_id. cost pipeline joins on trace_id -> metrics, ended up as 'unknown-org'.

linh nguyen: ouch. So sampling point matters. We discussed either: 1) enrich earlier (collector) with low-cardinality billing keys, 2) carry a deterministic hashed billing_key in headers so even sampled traces have it, or 3) do offline join using logs+metrics but that's heavier.

devon cho: quick pros/cons: enrich-at-ingest -> low perf overhead but requires safe low-cardinality key set and KMS if PII. header-propagation -> cheap but brittle if services forget to forward. offline-join -> accurate but increases storage and join complexity and latency for cost reports.

miguel ramos: Also watch out for cardinality explosion if we include model_variant + prompt_hash as billing keys. Need to restrict to org_id / billing_profile / route.

samir patel: Proposal: (a) require services to propagate a deterministic `billing_key` header (sha256(org_id + "|" + billing_profile)), (b) collector will always extract billing_key and persist it into trace root as `billing.key` (low cardinality), (c) sampler must be sampling-aware and prefer keeping traces that have billing.key present, (d) fallback: if trace lacks billing.key, use metric-side attribution heuristics.

linh nguyen: I like deterministic header + collector enrichment. A couple of notes: we must provide client libraries that automatically set the header to avoid dev ops mistakes. Also document allowed sources for billing_key and max cardinality (e.g., < 50k active keys).

anna kim: Agree. Also: we need to decide where hashing happens. If services hash locally they never send raw org_id -> better for privacy. But then we must ensure hash namespace/versioning.

miguel ramos: suggest header format `x-rw-billing: v1:<hex>` so we can rotate/upgrade hashing. Collector will validate `v1:` prefix and store raw header value as `billing.key.v1`.

devon cho: On the sampling algorithm: we should bias-sample traces with rare billing keys (low volume customers) higher to avoid missing their cost spikes. That complicates weighting but is doable in sampler.

samir patel: Implementation questions: where to do enrich? In our current collector (ingest fleet) or later in the pipeline (enrich service)? I prefer ingest fleet because we already mutate root attributes there and it keeps downstream cheaper.

linh nguyen: Ingest fleet is fine, but make sure enrich is idempotent (replay + reingest). Also log a soft-fail when header missing so we can measure adoption.

observability-bot: automated note: created tracking ticket OP-2357 to add header validation + collector extraction.

anna kim: I drafted small config sample for client libs:

```
# pseudocode (python)
import hashlib
raw = f"{org_id}|{billing_profile}"
key = hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]  # keep short to limit cardinality
headers['x-rw-billing'] = f"v1:{key}"
```

samir patel: Minor tweak: use 20 hex chars to reduce collision probability. Also record schema version in collector metadata.

miguel ramos: storage impact: adding billing.key to trace root increases indexable tag count. We'll mark it as low-cardinality in trace index config and avoid creating individual tag series in metrics store.

devon cho: For cost pipeline, algorithm: attribute token-level cost to billing.key if present else fallback to route-level attribution. We'll emit a warning metric `cost.attribution.fallback` when fallback used.

linh nguyen: How about traces that cross tenants (multi-tenant inference batch)? Need explicit per-request itemization from the app layer to map to billing keys; collector can't guess.

anna kim: Good point — add guidance: batch processors must emit per-item subspans with `billing.key` or use request-level breakdowns to be billed correctly. We'll add tests in our e2e suite.

samir patel: Next steps: 1) ship client libs with header helper + docs, 2) collector change to extract/store `billing.key.v1`, 3) sampler change to prefer retain traces with billing.key, 4) cost pipeline fallback metric and heuristics, 5) add e2e tests for batching.

miguel ramos: timeline?

anna kim: propose prototype + metric in 2 weeks, roll out libs in 4 weeks, collector deploy in 6 weeks (staged).

devon cho: I'll own sampler changes. samir you ok to own collector side?

samir patel: yep. I'll open PRs and link OP-2357.

linh nguyen: I'll draft docs + add adoption dashboard with missing-header rate.

anna kim: Great — thanks all. Tagging infra: @devex for client lib templates, @security for review of hashing/PII. :thumbsup:

observability-bot: linked OP-2357 -> https://tracker.internal/OP-2357
